summary: notification-service's repeated OOMKilled restarts (exit 137) are a self-consistent ~23h sawtooth memory leak whose onset is co-located with dep-5402 (v3.8.0, 2026-03-21T00:00Z), which added an in-process TemplateCache (ConcurrentHashMap) on the render path with no bound/TTL/eviction visible anywhere in the deploy or config record. Memory ramps gradually and monotonically from ~48% to ~98% over ~22h and resets on restart, verified across all three cycles (3/21, 3/22, 3/23), and the pre-deploy baseline (3/20) is flat and reset-free with zero restarts before 3/21T22:59:50Z. The reported "Kafka replay after maintenance" narrative is contradicted: memory was already ~88% at 16:00Z and rising well before the 18:00Z cfg-2410 retention change, the lag spikes FOLLOW the OOM rather than precede it, the co-consumer settlement-service stayed flat, and identical cycles ran on 3/21 and 3/22 before any 3/23 change. Confidence is medium (~0.70): the top hypothesis is clearly ahead and no competing hypothesis names a different origin, but the load-bearing claim that the cache is effectively unbounded is inference from absence of parameters (the dep-5402 diff/implementation is not retrievable) and the pre-deploy baseline covers only ~1 day.

ranked_hypotheses.title: In-memory TemplateCache introduced by dep-5402 grows without bound/without effective eviction until OOM
ranked_hypotheses.statement: dep-5402 (notification-service v3.8.0, 2026-03-21T00:00Z) added an in-process ConcurrentHashMap TemplateCache on the render path. Because no size bound/TTL/eviction policy is configured for it (and no config or deploy change anywhere in the window sets or removes one), heap occupancy climbs monotonically over roughly one day from ~48% to ~98%, old-gen saturates with long full GCs, and the container is OOMKilled (exit 137). The restart resets memory to ~48% and the cycle repeats at ~23h, delaying trade-confirmation emails. Cache growth is the dominant leak mechanism; the exact fraction of the ramp attributable to the cache versus other allocation paths is unresolved, and 'no bound configured' is absence-of-mention rather than proof of absence.

causal_chain.claim: dep-5402 adds an in-memory TemplateCache (ConcurrentHashMap keyed template+locale+userSegment) on the render path; the record states no size bound, TTL or eviction and shows status live / rolled_back_at null
No configuration anywhere in this service or the estate bounds a cache: notification-service has zero config changes, and the only estate-wide change is Kafka retention
The cache accumulates entries with zero evictions and grows to 188100 entries (single sample), and the app logs sustained old-gen heap-over-90 WARNs with full GCs up to 6488ms
Heap grows monotonically roughly 48%->98% per ~22h cycle, with max 98.44%; growth onset is co-located with the dep-5402 activation boundary versus a flat ~47-48% pre-deploy period
The container hits its memory limit and is OOMKilled with exit code 137 (same pod notification-service-7d9f), then restarts
After the restart, memory resets to ~48% and lag bursts in the bucket straddling the OOM then drains back to normal — lag is an effect of the restart, not the cause
The ~23h ramp-and-OOM cycle repeats across 3/21, 3/22 and 3/23 with the same pre-OOM old-gen signature, producing delayed trade-confirmation emails

assumptions: The TemplateCache is effectively unbounded in practice (no max-size/TTL/eviction in the deploy record, no config applied); evictions=0 at a bounded high-water mark would look identical at the sparse samples available — the cache implementation/diff is not retrievable (F20/F21/F22/F23 are absence-of-mention, not proof of absence)
The 188100-entry key space is not simply a bounded high-water mark (templates x locales x segments cardinality was never obtained; F24 says key-space cardinality is unquantified)

The ~23h OOM cycle did NOT exist before dep-5402; pre-3/20 memory telemetry is absent from the store (F26/F31), so 'no pre-existing cycle' is only established from 2026-03-20 onward plus the zero-restart fact back to 3/20 (F28)
The memory ramp is dominated by cache growth rather than the consumer/batch path (unquantified: no bytes-per-entry, one cache sample, F43)

ranked_hypotheses.title: Kafka maintenance is a red herring: lag spikes are the effect of notification-service restarting (corollary of H1, not an independent origin)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The consumer lag spikes reported as the symptom do not cause the OOM; they are caused by it. Each OOMKill freezes the consumer, lag accumulates in the bucket straddling the kill, and the restarted pod drains the backlog back to normal. The 3/23 Kafka retention change is coincidental and had no causal role — memory was already ~88% before it and rising. This is best read as a supporting observation about ordering (lag follows OOM, config change coincidental) rather than a competing root origin, since it names no independent cause; it is retained as the surviving non-broker reading of the lag symptom.

causal_chain.claim: Memory ramps monotonically to the limit and the pod is OOMKilled
Before the 3/23 change memory was already ~88% at 16:00Z and rose through 18:00Z without inflection — the maintenance did not create or amplify growth
20-min zoom shows lag normal (~60-77) until the restart, then exploding in the bucket straddling the OOM
Lag bursts recur tied to the restart cycle (same ~20:00/22:00 hours across days), not to load or maintenance events
The co-consumer settlement-service on the same shared broker stays flat and low across the same window, so no broker-wide replay drove the burst

assumptions: The lag-vs-OOM ordering established at 20-min resolution for the 3/21 restart holds for 3/23 as well (the 3/23 fine-grained lag query failed with 503; the 3/23 ordering rests on 2h buckets)
Lag bursts fully drain without manual intervention, consistent with restart-triggered backlog

ranked_hypotheses.title: Memory growth originates in the consumer/render path rather than the cache (cache bounded or incidental); leak origin unattributed
ranked_hypotheses.statement: dep-5402 changed the render path and its memory profile, but the growth driver is NOT (or not predominantly) the TemplateCache: either the cache key-space is effectively bounded (templates x locales x userSegments) so 188100 is a high-water mark with no evictions needed, or the dominant allocation is on the consumer/message-processing path that dep-5402 altered. In that reading dep-5402 remains the most likely trigger (growth onset is co-located with its activation) but the specific mechanism inside the release is unattributed, and the fix is not 'make the cache bounded' but re-instrumenting and reverting/patching the release. This hypothesis exists to carry the case the critic flags: if the cache is bounded, H1's stated mechanism collapses to a temporal association.

causal_chain.claim: dep-5402 is the only change co-located with growth onset; pre-deploy 3/20 memory is flat at ~48% with zero restarts
The cache's key space may be intrinsically bounded (templates x locales x segments) so a no-eviction high-water mark is expected and 188100 need not imply unbounded growth
Per-cycle cache maximum is obtainable for only one of three cycles, and the high-water sample resets toward ~0 after restart, so cache growth is not proven to track the heap ramp
The ramp could instead be a slow accumulation on the consumer/render path introduced by the same release; no bytes-per-entry or component breakdown exists to separate the two
Either way the pod reaches ~98% and is OOMKilled on a ~23h cycle, then resets and repeats

assumptions: The TemplateCache key space is bounded and the observed size=188100 with evictions=0 is a legitimate high-water mark (cardinality never retrieved)
The consumer/render path inside dep-5402 could allocate cumulatively (e.g. per-message retained state) — no code or diff is retrievable to confirm or deny

ranked_hypotheses.title: Kafka maintenance (retention change cfg-2410) triggered a consumer replay that OOMKilled the pod
ranked_hypotheses.statement: cfg-2410 reduced broker log retention 7d->3d at 2026-03-23T18:00Z; the maintenance event caused notification-service's consumer to replay/re-read messages, buffering them in memory and OOMing roughly 2h later.

causal_chain.claim: cfg-2410 changes the shared kafka broker retention 7d->3d at 18:00Z on 3/23 and is the only change that day
The maintenance event causes the notification-service consumer to replay/rebuffer messages (no offset-reset, reassignment or broker restart event appears in the change feed — assumed)
Replayed messages accumulate in memory producing an abrupt spike and OOM (assumed)
Pod OOMKilled ~2h later at 19:59:21Z

assumptions: A consumer replay actually occurred after the retention change
HIST-104's rebalance-storm mechanism (which produced identical lag+delayed-email symptoms) recurred here
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Timing and mechanism both fail on verified evidence. Memory was already ~88% at 16:00Z and rising monotonically before the 18:00Z change (F14/F13); the OOM fired 1h59m after the change while already near limit. Growth is a gradual ~22h ramp, not the abrupt spike a replay burst requires (F9/F12). The identical ~23h OOM cycle ran on 3/21 and 3/22, before the 3/23 change and even the 3/22 auth deploy (F19/F7), and the pre-deploy 3/20 baseline is flat with zero restarts (F27/F28). Lag follows the restart per 20-min zoom (F10/F17), and the co-consumer settlement-service on the same broker stayed flat with no replay symptom (F18). The replay half of the chain is entirely unverified; the change feed is a config/deploy feed rather than a broker event log, so absence there is weak — but the verified timing/shape/scope contradictions carry the rejection independently.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Shared broker / node-level resource change drove memory pressure; notification-service is the loudest victim
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A cluster/node/broker-level resource change increased memory pressure affecting notification-service, with the OOM a local consequence of shared infrastructure degradation.

causal_chain.claim: A shared broker/maintenance event affects consuming services
Elevated memory/lag pressure manifests on notification-service (assumed)
notification-service OOMs

assumptions: A broker/node-level resource change existed beyond the retention setting — none is observable in the change feed
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: The only change in the estate is the retention value (F1/F23); no node/broker resource change is observable. settlement-service on the same shared broker showed flat, low lag with no symptom (F18). notification-service is not a shared node (F4), and its memory ramp starts at its own deploy boundary (F15) and was already near limit before the maintenance (F14), not at any infra event. The pre-deploy baseline is itself flat with zero restarts (F27/F28), leaving no infra signal.

facts.statement: Three and only three OOMKilled restarts of notification-service occurred in the 7-day window, all same pod notification-service-7d9f with exit code 137: 2026-03-21T22:59:50Z, 2026-03-22T21:59:47Z and 2026-03-23T19:59:21Z; the cumulative restarts metric independently steps 0→1→2→3 in the matching hour buckets.

Memory grew gradually and monotonically before each restart (leak ramp, not an abrupt spike): 3/22 00:00 50.33% → 20:00 94.91% → 22:00 reset to 48.25%; 3/23 00:00 52.99% → 18:00 95.05% → 20:00 reset to 48.33%, max 98.44%.

Before dep-5402 the baseline is flat and reset-free: over 2026-03-20T00:00Z..2026-03-21T00:00Z memory_pct mean 48.06, min 42.73, max 54.77 across 42 buckets with no monotonic climb, and the cumulative restarts metric is 0.0 for every 1h bucket from 3/20T00:00Z through 3/21T22:00Z.

Onset of the ramp is co-located with the dep-5402 activation boundary: memory is steady at ~47-48% through 2026-03-20 and at 2026-03-21T00:00Z, then climbs cleanly (47.48% → 50.54% → 53.39% in 80-min steps) to 94.99% at 21:20Z.

There is no OOMKilled or restart event on notification-service before 2026-03-21T22:59:50Z: a log search over 2026-03-10T00:00Z..2026-03-21T22:59:50Z for 'OOM' and for 'restart' returns exactly that one line each, and no earlier event exists.

Exactly two deployments landed in the 03-16..03-23 window: dep-5402 notification-service v3.8.0 on 2026-03-21T00:00:00Z ('Add in-memory template cache for email rendering'; changes 'TemplateCache (ConcurrentHashMap) keyed by template+locale+userSegment' and 'render path uses cache'; status live, rolled_back_at null) and dep-5415 auth-service v7.1.4 on 3/22 ('bump jackson').

The dep-5402 record contains no size/eviction/TTL parameter anywhere; no other in-window deployment carries a cache-size/eviction diff; and a service-scoped config query for notification-service over 2026-03-01..2026-03-23 returns count 0.

The app logged 'TemplateCache stats: size=188100 entries, evictions=0' at 18:54:31Z on 3/23 plus 10 WARN lines 'heap usage N% over 90 (old gen), full GC took N ms' (up to 6488ms) between 18:34Z and 19:49Z, all before the 19:59:21Z OOM; evictions=0 in all three retrievable cache samples (18:54:31Z, 21:00:44Z, 22:00:34Z).
The 3/21 restart shows the same pre-OOM signature as 3/23: 16 old-gen heap-overflow WARNs (full GC up to 8220ms) from 21:37Z, with the restart at 22:59:50Z.

The 3/23 OOM fired at 2026-03-23T19:59:21Z, 1h59m after the 18:00Z Kafka maintenance, while the pod was already at ~96% memory; on 20-min buckets memory was already ~88% at 16:00Z and rose monotonically to 95.96% at 19:00Z and 96.73%/98.44% at 19:40Z, then reset to 46.72% at 20:00Z.

The only configuration change in the whole estate during 2026-03-16..2026-03-23 is cfg-2410 on the shared kafka broker: log.retention.ms 604800000 → 259200000 (7d → 3d) at 2026-03-23T18:00:00Z; no memory-limit, consumer/batch or JVM/runtime config change appears for any service, and no deployments were recorded on 3/23 itself.

Consumer lag does not lead the OOM: on 3/21 a 20-min zoom shows lag normal (~60-77) through 22:20 and only exploding in the 22:40 bucket (avg 4334.88, max 17161.92) after the 22:59:50Z restart; on 3/23 lag is normal (~49-71) through 19:30Z and only bursts in the 19:45Z bucket (avg 6082.94, max 18137.93) and 20:00Z bucket (avg 10696.07), returning to ~64/50 by 20:30-20:45Z.

The lag burst is not a shared-broker/replay symptom: settlement-service, the other consumer on the shared kafka broker, shows flat low lag (avg 32-56, max 82.06) across the same 18:00-23:00Z window with no spike at 19:45-20:00Z.

notification-service's dependency edges are only kafka (queue-consume) and email-provider (external, no telemetry); notification-service is not a shared node (shared:false), and the only shared node in its graph is kafka. There is no cache/datastore node behind TemplateCache — it is purely in-process.

notification-service exposes no cache metric: a cache_size query returns not_found with available_metrics = ['consumer_lag','cpu_pct','error_rate','latency_p99_ms','memory_pct','request_rate','restarts']; the only cache-size signal is the sparse INFO log line (3 samples in 72h).

After the 3/23 restart the cache size drops from the 18:54:31Z high-water mark of 188100 to 9000 (21:00:44Z) and 18000 (22:00:34Z) — a reset toward zero, not a sustained plateau; per-cycle max is reportable for only one of the three cycles (3/23).

Historical precedent for notification-service's reported symptoms is HIST-104 (2025-11-05) 'notification-service lag after Kafka broker rebalance' (rebalance storm, not an OOM/leak cycle), and no prior OOM/unbounded-cache/memory-sawtooth incident exists for this service in the retrieved records.

Data-availability limits: memory_pct has no coverage before 2026-03-20T00:00Z (query for 03-10..03-18 returns points=[] with data_range start=2026-03-20), and the deployment/ticket record contains zero notification-service entries before 2026-03-21, so the pre-3/21 period is absent rather than documented clean.

assumptions: The TemplateCache is effectively unbounded in practice: no max-size/TTL/eviction parameter appears in the dep-5402 record, no config was ever applied to the service, and evictions=0 at every retrievable sample — but this is absence-of-mention plus one sparse sample, not proof, since the cache implementation/diff is not retrievable and a bounded no-eviction high-water mark would look identical at these samples (F20, F21, F22, F40, F41).
The 188100-entry key space (template x locale x userSegment) is not simply a bounded high-water mark; the cardinality of that key space was never retrieved (F24, F43).

The ~23h OOM cycle did not exist before dep-5402: pre-2026-03-20 memory telemetry is absent and the deployment/config record is silent before 2026-03-21, so this is established only from 2026-03-20 onward plus zero restarts back to 3/20 (F26, F27, F28, F31, F36).

The memory ramp is dominated by TemplateCache growth rather than the consumer/batch path altered by dep-5402: there is no bytes-per-entry data, only one cache-size sample per cycle, and no cache metric (F16, F41, F43).

The lag-vs-OOM ordering established at 20-min resolution for the 3/21 restart holds for the 3/23 event as well; the 3/23 fine-grained lag query failed (503) so its ordering rests on 2h buckets (F10, F17).
The reported symptom 'consumer lag spikes' reflects restart-induced backlog that drains without manual intervention, consistent with the observed return to baseline lag by 20:30-20:45Z (F17).

The single cache stat sample and the single 0.70-confidence mechanism reading are representative of the leak's behaviour across all three cycles, even though cycles 1 and 2 have zero cache samples (F38, F43).

timeline.event: Pre-deploy baseline begins: memory_pct flat at mean 48.06% (min 42.73, max 54.77) across 42 buckets over ~24h, no monotonic climb, and cumulative restarts metric is 0.0 through 2026-03-21T22:00Z.

dep-5402 lands: notification-service v3.8.0 'Add in-memory template cache for email rendering' (TemplateCache ConcurrentHashMap keyed by template+locale+userSegment; render path uses cache); no size/TTL/eviction parameter in the record. Memory is steady at ~47-48% at this boundary and then begins a clean linear climb.
Memory reaches 94.99% at the end of the 3/21 ramp (47.48% → 50.54% → 53.39% in 80-min steps from the deploy boundary).
Pre-OOM old-gen pressure begins on the first cycle: 16 WARN 'heap usage over 90 (old gen)' lines with full GC up to 8220ms.

First OOMKilled restart (pod notification-service-7d9f, exit 137). Consumer lag is normal (~60-77) through 22:20 and only explodes in the 22:40 bucket (avg 4334.88, max 17161.92) after the restart — lag follows the OOM.
dep-5415 auth-service v7.1.4 ('bump jackson') lands — the only other in-window deploy, containing no cache-size/eviction change.
Second cycle peak/drain: memory 94.91% at 20:00, lag burst (avg 790.21, max 17611.66), reset to 48.25% at 22:00 after the 21:59:47Z OOMKill; cadence ~23h.
Memory already ~88% on 3/23 and rising — approximately two hours BEFORE the Kafka maintenance, so the config change did not create or inflect the growth.

cfg-2410 applied at the shared kafka broker: log.retention.ms 604800000 → 259200000 (7d → 3d), the only config change in the whole estate for the window and the only change on the incident day; no deployments were recorded on 3/23.
Ten WARN 'heap usage over 90 (old gen)' lines with full GC up to 6488ms appear between 18:34Z and 19:49Z, before the OOM, and continue through the 18:00Z config change.
App logs 'TemplateCache stats: size=188100 entries, evictions=0' — the single highest cache sample, ~1h05m before the OOM.
Consumer lag still normal (~49-71) while memory approaches its limit (96.73%/98.44% at 19:40Z) — lag does not precede the OOM.

Lag bursts only as the pod dies: 19:45Z bucket avg 6082.94 / max 18137.93 and 20:00Z bucket avg 10696.07, straddling the restart; settlement-service on the same shared broker stays flat (avg 32-56, max 82.06) across 18:00-23:00Z.
Third OOMKilled restart (exit 137), 1h59m after the 18:00Z Kafka retention change and ~2h20m before the incident report; memory resets to 46.72% in the 20:00Z bucket.
Incident INC-004 reported by on-call SRE: third OOM restart this week, trade-confirmation emails delayed ~25 min, narrative attributes the OOM to a Kafka replay after maintenance.
Lag returns to baseline (~64/50) by 20:30-20:45Z, consistent with a restart-triggered backlog draining, not a persistent replay.
Post-restart cache size drops to 9000 entries (evictions=0), then 18000 at 22:00:34Z — a reset toward zero rather than a sustained plateau; per-cycle max is obtainable only for this cycle.

recommended_actions.action: Immediate mitigation (safe, no-open-fork): revert or roll back notification-service release v3.8.0 (dep-5402, 2026-03-21T00:00Z) to the pre-3/21 build, i.e. remove the in-process TemplateCache from the render path. If a full rollback is not possible, deploy a bounded TemplateCache (max-size/TTL/LRU eviction) plus a JVM heap limit/headroom change as a compensating control, and raise the container memory limit only as a temporary stopgap since it would merely lengthen the ~23h cycle.
recommended_actions.rationale: The leak onset is co-located with dep-5402's activation (F2, F15), the ramp is gradual and monotonic to ~98% with reset-on-restart across all three cycles (F9, F15, F19), and the only cache-bearing change in the window is dep-5402 with no bound/TTL/eviction recorded (F20, F21, F22, F32). Removing it removes the mechanism regardless of whether the internal allocation path is the cache or another dep-5402-altered path (H5 keeps dep-5402 as the trigger, so the fix direction is unchanged).

recommended_actions.action: Immediate: do NOT execute a Kafka change as the primary mitigation. If any broker-side action was being considered on the strength of the 'replay' narrative, cancel it — cfg-2410 / log.retention.ms is not indicated.
recommended_actions.rationale: Memory was already ~88% at 16:00Z and rising before the 18:00Z retention change (F14, F13); the OOM fired 1h59m later while already near limit (F13); identical cycles ran on 3/21 and 3/22 before any 3/23 change (F19, F7); and the co-consumer settlement-service stayed flat across the window, ruling out a broker-wide replay (F18). A retention change is a one-way, low-benefit action here.

recommended_actions.action: Short term: add a cache metric (cache_size, evictions, hit/miss) and emit bounded-cardinality TemplateCache stats on a fixed interval (e.g. every 1-5 min) for notification-service, since the only obtainable signal is a sparse INFO log line with 3 samples in 72h.
recommended_actions.rationale: notification-service exposes no cache metric (available_metrics = consumer_lag, cpu_pct, error_rate, latency_p99_ms, memory_pct, request_rate, restarts), so the plateau-vs-monotonic question can only ever be answered from sparse logs (F41, F38, F39, F43). Instrumentation is what would convert the remaining inference (cache unboundedness) into a measured fact.

recommended_actions.action: Short term: after the revert, verify by observing memory_pct over at least two full cycle periods (~48h) that the ramp-then-reset sawtooth is gone and the pre-deploy flat ~48% band is restored, with zero OOMKilled/exit-137 events and no repeat of the 18:34-19:49Z old-gen 'over 90 / full GC' WARN cluster.
recommended_actions.rationale: The 3/20 baseline was flat (mean 48.06%, no reset-to-low sawtooth) with zero restarts, and the ramp onset tracks the dep-5402 boundary (F27, F28, F15); a post-revert flat baseline with zero restarts confirms the fix. The pre-OOM old-gen WARN pattern is the signature to watch (F16, F19).

recommended_actions.action: Short term: quantify the residual uncertainty with one targeted check per open question — (a) retrieve the dep-5402 diff/implementation or the TemplateCache class to confirm the eviction policy, and (b) obtain the cardinality of template x locale x userSegment to judge whether 188100 entries is an unbounded high-water mark; if (a)/(b) show a properly bounded cache, escalate to re-instrumenting and re-attributing rather than treating cache growth as the proven mechanism.
recommended_actions.rationale: The single genuinely unverified hop in H1 is whether the cache is unbounded: size=188100/evictions=0 cannot distinguish unbounded growth from a bounded no-eviction high-water mark, and the key-space cardinality was never obtained (F16, F20, F24, F40, F43). H5 keeps dep-5402 as the trigger but disputes the internal mechanism, so this check discriminates H1's mechanism from H5 without changing the fix direction.

recommended_actions.action: Long term: add a mandatory cache-bound requirement to the notification-service render path (explicit max entries/TTL/eviction) and gate future in-memory cache introductions behind a leak/soak test that runs through at least one full cycle period before release, plus a memory-usage alert that fires on a monotonic climb trend rather than only at the ~90% static threshold.
recommended_actions.rationale: The failure mode was a monotonic climb over ~22h to OOM (F9, F12); the existing alerts only surfaced as 'heap usage over 90 (old gen)' when the leak was already within ~1-2h of the kill (F16, F19), so trade-confirmation emails were delayed ~25 min. A trend-based alert plus a pre-release soak test prevents recurrence.

data_gaps: The dep-5402 diff/implementation and source code are not retrievable, and there is no cache-size/eviction config anywhere, so whether the TemplateCache is actually bounded cannot be directly confirmed — the strongest remaining inference is the absence of a bound plus the single sample at size=188100/evictions=0, which cannot distinguish unbounded growth from a bounded no-eviction high-water mark.

Key-space cardinality (templates x locales x userSegments) was never retrieved (budget exhausted), so whether 188100 entries is a plausible unbounded high-water mark or a bounded plateau remains unresolved.

notification-service exposes no cache metric, so no continuous size-vs-heap series can be constructed; only 3 cache-size log samples exist in 72h, and per-cycle max is obtainable for only cycle 3 — the question 'is per-cycle max constant or increasing?' is not answerable.

The pre-3/21 baseline covers only ~1 day (2026-03-20); memory_pct has no coverage before 2026-03-20T00:00Z and the deployment/ticket record has zero notification-service entries before 2026-03-21, so 'the ~23h cycle did not exist before dep-5402' is established for 3/20 onward only, not the full requested window. A pre-existing restart/leak cadence cannot be positively excluded before 3/21.

The 20-min lag ordering for the 3/23 restart (the reported incident day) failed with 503 and rests on 2h buckets; the fine-grained ordering proof comes from the 3/21 restart with an identical restart signature.

The exact container memory limit in bytes and RSS/heap breakdown were unavailable (memory measured as percent only), so the absolute limit and whether it was unchanged across the three cycles cannot be stated.

No application-level ERROR/exception logs beyond the three OOMKilled container messages were retrievable (total_matched=3), so any consumer/replay or allocation errors logged at WARN/INFO were not inspected.

The wide-window log search for the string 'TemplateCache' over 2026-03-21..2026-03-23 returned total_matched=0 while a narrowed 4-minute INFO query matched — it is undetermined whether cache-stat logging only started on 3/23 or the wide query failed to match, so nothing is known about cache size on cycles 1 and 2.
Whether notification-service's memory ceiling or JVM heap limit was ever raised/lowered could not be determined (no consumer/batch-size or JVM heap-limit settings in dependency queries).

A broker-side restart, partition reassignment or consumer-group offset-reset during the 3/23 maintenance is not observable in the change feed (only the retention value appears), so a broker-side event that would produce a consumer replay could not be positively ruled in or out from those feeds.

Searches for other services' (order-service, kafka, email-provider) memory/lag/error trends were not executed or failed (tool-call budget, not_found for 'trade-service'/'email-service'), so whether the incident is isolated to notification-service or part of a broader platform memory/lag issue is unanswered.

Historical incident search and deployment history are keyword/limit-bounded and partly failed (503/timeout), so the full pre-3/21 history of notification-service is unverified; 'no prior OOM/unbounded-cache precedent' rests on the retrieved records only.
what_would_change_the_conclusion: Retrieving the dep-5402 diff/implementation showing the TemplateCache is properly bounded (explicit max-size/TTL/LRU eviction) — this would collapse H1's stated mechanism (unbounded cache growth) to a temporal association and shift weight to H5 (growth originates in the consumer/render path changed by dep-5402, mechanism unattributed).

Obtaining the template x locale x userSegment cardinality and finding it is naturally bounded at ~188100 with a documented no-eviction high-water mark and no growth after that point — the size=188100/evictions=0 sample would then be a legitimate plateau rather than evidence of unbounded growth.

Evidence that the ~23h ramp-and-reset OOM cycle existed before dep-5402 (e.g. recovered memory_pct or restart records for 2026-03-10..2026-03-19, or earlier deployment/config history showing a pre-3/21 cache or leak) — this would break H1's causal claim and make the leak a pre-existing/unattributed origin.
A cache-size series (or per-cycle max for cycles 1 and 2) showing per-cycle max constant or decreasing rather than growing with heap, which would decouple cache growth from the memory ramp.

A verified broker-side event (partition reassignment, consumer-group offset reset, broker restart) during the 3/23 18:00Z maintenance, plus a demonstrated replay with an abrupt memory spike, which would revive the replay mechanism.

Fine-grained (20-min) 3/23 lag data showing lag rising BEFORE the memory ramp inflection (rather than straddling the restart as observed on 3/21), which would flip the lag-vs-OOM ordering on the incident day.

findings.statement: Exactly three OOMKilled restarts of notification-service occurred in the 7-day window, at 2026-03-21T22:59:50Z, 2026-03-22T21:59:47Z and 2026-03-23T19:59:21Z (same pod notification-service-7d9f, exit code 137).

The cumulative restarts metric steps 0→1 in the 2026-03-21T22:00 bucket, 1→2 in the 2026-03-22T22:00 bucket, and 2→3 in the 2026-03-23T20:00 bucket, independently confirming three restart events at those hours.

Memory grew gradually and monotonically before each restart (leak/burst ramp, not an abrupt spike): e.g. 2026-03-22 00:00 50.33% → 20:00 94.91% → 22:00 reset to 48.25%; and 2026-03-23 00:00 52.99% → 18:00 95.05% → 20:00 reset to 48.33%, with max reaching 98.44%.

A ~2h-bucket view makes consumer_lag look like it spikes in the same bucket as each restart (e.g. 2026-03-21T22:00 avg 2273.11, max 17161.92), but a 20-min zoom shows the spike follows the OOM: lag is normal (~60-77) through 22:20 and only explodes in the 22:40 bucket (avg 4334.88, max 17161.92) after the 22:59 restart.

Notable lag spikes recur in the same ~22:00/20:00 hours across days: 2026-03-21T22:00 max 17161.92, 2026-03-22T20:00 avg 790.21 max 17611.66 / 22:00 avg 1589.77, 2026-03-23T18:00 avg 810.33 max 18137.93 / 20:00 avg 1542.68 — i.e. the lag bursts are tied to the restart cycle, not to a baseline load shift.

Because memory ramps ~48%→~98% across a full ~22h and the lag only bursts at the restart, the reported 'consumer choking on a Kafka replay right after maintenance' narrative does not match a replay burst (which would show an abrupt memory spike). The pattern is a steady per-cycle memory growth culminating in OOM.

All three OOMKilled events are the same pod/same signature (exit code 137, container notification-service-7d9f), and the 3/23 event fired at 2026-03-23T19:59:21Z — 1h59m AFTER the 18:00Z Kafka maintenance — while the pod was already at ~96% memory. So the OOM was not triggered at maintenance time; memory was already near limit 2h before.

Zoomed to 20-min buckets on 2026-03-23, memory was already ~88% at 16:00Z and rose monotonically to 95.96% at 19:00Z and 96.73%/98.44% at 19:40Z, then reset to 46.72% in the 20:00 bucket. The ramp therefore began well before the 18:00Z Kafka retention change and continued through it — the config change did not create or inflect the growth.

The 3/21 cycle shows the ramp starting right at the 2026-03-21T00:00Z deploy-5402 boundary (steady 47-48% through 2026-03-20 and at 3/21T00:00, then a clean linear climb from 47.48% → 50.54% → 53.39% in 80-min steps up to 94.99% at 21:20Z), whereas the 3/20 period before the deploy is flat at ~47-48%. Growth onset is therefore co-located with dep-5402's activation, not with the 3/18-3/19 baseline.

The log evidence for the ramp is a template-cache stat and sustained old-gen pressure, not Kafka replay: at 18:54:31Z on 3/23 the app logged 'TemplateCache stats: size=188100 entries, evictions=0' and 10 WARN lines 'heap usage N% over 90 (old gen), full GC took N ms' (up to 6488ms) between 18:34Z and 19:49Z, all before the 19:59:21Z OOM. Unbounded cache with 0 evictions is the literal growth mechanism.

findings.statement: Consumer lag does NOT lead the 3/23 OOM: lag is normal (~49-71) through 19:30Z and only bursts in the 19:45Z bucket (avg 6082.94, max 18137.93) and 20:00Z bucket (avg 10696.07) i.e. straddling the 19:59:21Z restart, returning to ~64/50 by 20:30-20:45Z. Lag is an effect of the restart, not the cause of the memory ramp.

The lag spike is NOT a shared-broker/replay symptom: settlement-service (the other consumer on the shared kafka broker) shows flat, low lag across the exact same 18:00-23:00Z window (avg 32-56, max 82.06), with no spike at 19:45-20:00Z when notification-service hit 18137.93. This argues the 3/23 lag burst is local to notification-service's own restart, not a broker-wide replay; Kafka maintenance was not needed to produce it.

The restart cadence is a self-consistent ~23h cycle, not a new event: cumulative restarts metric steps to 1 in the 2026-03-21T22:40Z bucket, to 2 in the 2026-03-22T20:00Z bucket and to 3 in the 2026-03-23T20:00Z bucket, and the 3/21 restart (22:59:50Z) also shows 16 old-gen heap-overflow WARNs (up to full GC 8220ms) from 21:37Z — the same pre-OOM signature as 3/23. This repetition pre-dates any 3/23 change and pre-dates the 3/22 auth-service deploy, so it cannot be caused by either.
